stories.head: Confronting the 'Experience Debt' That Derails Your Customer Journey
stories.plain: SAS strategist Jonathan Moran explains how experience debt builds up each time a legacy system is left unmodified, quietly degrading the customer journey. For MarTech buyers, it frames a real cost to inaction on platform modernization and helps justify investment in updated customer engagement infrastructure.

stories.head: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons
stories.plain: Intuit is selling Mailchimp — one of the world's best-known email marketing platforms — to Bending Spoons, the Italian app company known for taking over faded tech brands. This is a major ownership shift for a platform used by millions of small businesses, and raises real questions about where Mailchimp's AI and automation roadmap goes next.

stories.head: Enterprise AI governance alone can't protect your brand — marketing-specific guardrails needed
stories.plain: Corporate IT-level AI governance policies are too broad to catch off-brand or legally risky content that marketing AI tools produce. The article argues marketers need their own layer of content guardrails — separate from enterprise policy — to stop embarrassing or harmful AI-generated output before it goes public. Directly shapes how AI creative is bought and governed.

stories.head: Constructor launches Commerce AEO to convert AI answer-engine visibility into retail sales
stories.plain: Constructor's new Commerce AEO product goes beyond just appearing in ChatGPT or Perplexity answers — it tracks whether those appearances actually drive purchases. This is one of the first tools to close the loop between generative engine visibility and revenue, making GEO measurable for e-commerce teams rather than just a vanity metric.

stories.head: The hidden risks of auto-generated creative: brand, legal, and regulatory exposure
stories.plain: A practical breakdown of the copyright, false-advertising, data-privacy, and brand-safety risks marketers face when publishing AI-generated images and copy. As AI content generation becomes routine in marketing workflows, this sets out the legal and governance checkpoints teams need before hitting publish — relevant to anyone buying or building genAI creative tools.

stories.head: SOCi launches MCP server to deepen integrations powering its agentic marketing workforce
stories.plain: SOCi is rolling out a Model Context Protocol server so its AI agents can pull live data from over 140 tools — Salesforce, Snowflake, Canva and more — without manual hand-offs. MCP is quickly becoming the connective tissue for agentic marketing stacks, and this launch signals how multi-location brands will wire AI agents into their existing data and content systems.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Purchase Funnel
body: AI agents are no longer just helping humans shop — they are increasingly making or heavily shaping purchase decisions on behalf of buyers. Constructor's Commerce AEO launch and research showing 72% of holiday shoppers using AI signal that brand visibility inside AI outputs is now a commercial requirement, not a nice-to-have.

This forces a structural rethink: optimising for AI agent consideration (AEO) sits alongside, and sometimes above, traditional SEO. Marketers must ask what signals — structured data, authoritative content, third-party validation — make an AI agent trust and recommend their brand, because a buyer's agent that never surfaces you is as bad as a search engine that never ranks you.
ev: MarTech · When AI agents evaluate B2B vendors
Agile Brand · 72% of shoppers use AI

themes.head: Deploying Agents Fast, Measuring Them Never
body: Organisations are shipping AI agents into production well ahead of any governance or measurement framework. The gap between deployment speed and accountability is widening — marketers have no reliable way to audit what agents decide, what they cost in brand equity, or whether they are even working.

Marketing ops teams are being asked to close this gap retroactively, turning agent readiness from a blind spot into a defensible capability. The practical implication: before the next agent goes live, teams need outcome definitions, escalation paths, and attribution hooks baked in — not bolted on after a problem surfaces.
ev: MarTech · Deploying agents faster than measuring them
MarTech · AI agents make CX marketing's problem

themes.head: AI Creative's Hidden Liability Iceberg
body: Auto-generated creative is moving from experiment to everyday production pipeline, but the brand, legal, and regulatory exposure underneath it is barely understood. Copyright ownership ambiguity, hallucinated claims, and regulatory non-compliance are real risks that enterprise AI governance policies alone cannot contain.

The story from multiple items this month is consistent: AI tools need your proprietary business knowledge and brand rules injected into them, or they produce output that is generically competent but specifically dangerous. This makes internal knowledge management and prompt governance a legal & compliance issue, not just a marketing quality issue.
ev: MarTech · Hidden risks of auto-generated creative
MarTech · Enterprise AI governance can't protect brand
MarTech · Even smartest AI needs business knowledge

themes.head: Attribution Is Structurally Broken Again
body: With AI-mediated touchpoints, zero-click answers, and agent-assisted purchases now embedded in the funnel, traditional multichannel attribution is missing decisions it cannot even see. The decisions that convert are increasingly happening in channels that leave no trackable signal — inside AI overviews, inside agents, inside conversations.

Emerging approaches — such as Tunnl's decision-layer measurement and cross-channel MMM frameworks built for AI-first media — suggest attribution must evolve from tracking clicks to inferring influence across dark-funnel interactions. Teams that cling to last-click or even multi-touch models will systematically misallocate budget as AI intermediaries multiply.
ev: Agile Brand · Measuring decisions attribution never saw

themes.head: Stack Consolidation Accelerates Under AI Pressure
body: The Mailchimp sale is the most visible signal of a broader consolidation wave: standalone marketing tools that cannot demonstrate clear AI-era value are being divested, acquired, or sunset. Forrester's framing of a 'software abundance' era — where AI dramatically lowers the cost to build features — means differentiation through unique capability is harder and competitive pressure on point solutions is relentless.

Simultaneously, platforms like Bloomreach (AthenaHQ acquisition), SOCi (MCP server), and GoEnhance AI are racing to build unified workflow layers rather than isolated features. The strategic signal for buyers: evaluate vendors on their integration & orchestration architecture, not just current feature parity, because the half-life of a standalone tool is shortening fast.
ev: MarTech · Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons
Agile Brand · Software abundance era, Forrester

month.takeaway: Every theme this month connects to the same underlying shift: AI intermediaries are absorbing the moments that used to be directly measurable, governed, and owned by marketers — forcing a simultaneous rethink of visibility strategy, measurement architecture, creative governance, and stack design.
